clue.text: Left us blocked by our CID, bumbling, absurd

parts.note: L is the standard abbreviation for left

indicators.note: something blocked has another thing jammed in the middle of it, so us is plugged by other letters

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: bumbling describes clumsy confused movement, so our CID lose their order

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A writer mocks the detectives of the local CID for their bungling, which leaves the public stuck.
explanation.walkthrough: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, Britain's plain-clothes police detectives; here the letters are just raw material.
explanation.definitionFit: Ludicrous and absurd are close synonyms, both meaning ridiculous or laughable.

clue.text: Nautical (at sea) skipping an area that's crazy

indicators.note: at sea means confused and all over the place, so the letters are jumbled
skipping means missing out, so one letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A maritime mission at sea that sails past a region it ought to visit seems mad.
explanation.walkthrough: Nautical loses one A, and the remaining letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Lunatic as an adjective means wildly foolish or mad, a synonym for crazy.

clue.text: Dust storm was rising

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means read upwards, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: lived means existed or was

explanation.surface: A dust storm was getting up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' looks like it describes the storm, but it signals the reversal in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A devil, or dust devil, is a whirlwind that lifts a column of sand or dust.

clue.text: Line brought in fish from the Arctic?

indicators.note: brought in means taken inside, so the line letter goes within the fish

parts.note: a cod is a fish
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A fishing line landing a catch from the Arctic Ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as an example: being from the Arctic suggests coldness.
explanation.definitionFit: Something from the Arctic, like an Arctic wind, is typically freezing, so the definition works by example.

clue.text: Charmingly fogyish over argument turning up between Lords

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for over

indicators.note: between places one item in the gap separating two others, here the pair of lords

parts.note: LD is the abbreviation for Lord, and the plural gives two of them

indicators.note: turning up in a down clue means flipping upwards, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: a row is an argument

explanation.surface: A cosy old-fashioned scene: a dispute flaring up among peers in the Lords.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural Lords supplies the abbreviation twice, one on each side of the reversed argument. The House of Lords is Britain's upper chamber of Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: Old-world means quaintly traditional and old-fashioned in an appealing way, which suits fogyish charm.

clue.text: Companion consumed, swallowed by pig

indicators.note: something swallowed ends up inside the swallower, so the pig word goes round the other

parts.note: a sow is a female pig
had means ate, as in had lunch

explanation.surface: A friend was eaten, gulped down by a hog: a grim farmyard tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Companion' sounds like a person, but a shadow is the companion that never leaves your side.
explanation.definitionFit: A shadow is someone who follows another closely everywhere, a constant companion.

clue.text: Anger about book, an authoritative text

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for anger wraps itself round the next item

parts.note: bile is bitter anger or ill-temper
B is the abbreviation for book

explanation.surface: Someone furious about a book that claims to be the last word on its subject.
explanation.walkthrough: BILE goes round B: BI-B-LE.
explanation.definitionFit: A bible is any work regarded as the definitive reference on a subject, like a cook's bible.

clue.text: One that may ring pop star, extracting money, implying poison

parts.note: a bell is something that rings

indicators.note: extracting means pulling out, so a letter is removed from the star's name

parts.note: Madonna, the American singer
M is the abbreviation for money

explanation.surface: A fan who telephones a pop star to wring cash out of her, hinting at poison.
explanation.walkthrough: MADONNA loses M, and BELL comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Belladonna, or deadly nightshade, is a highly toxic plant and the poison extracted from it.

clue.text: Polluting modified biofuel? No good

indicators.note: modified means changed in form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written
N is the abbreviation for no
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Is a modified green fuel still polluting? Then it's no good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No good' looks like a verdict, but it supplies two letters for the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: To befoul is to make filthy or dirty, so befouling means contaminating, which is polluting.

clue.text: City to suspend importing sulphur drug

parts.note: EC is the postcode area for the City of London

indicators.note: importing means bringing in, so the suspend word takes a letter inside it

parts.note: to stay a judgment or execution is to suspend it
S is the chemical symbol for sulphur

explanation.surface: A city halts the import of a sulphur-based drug.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is London's financial district, whose postcode district letters are the first two of the answer. To stay an execution is to suspend it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecstasy is the street name of the recreational drug MDMA.

clue.text: Unprofitable bottling bit of vodka, on reflection, producing depression

indicators.note: a reflection shows things the wrong way round, so the result is read backwards
to bottle something is to hold it inside, so the first word encloses the next

parts.note: a lean year is an unprofitable one

indicators.note: a bit of a word is a single letter of it, here its opening one

parts.note: the opening letter of vodka

explanation.surface: A drinks business finds bottling vodka loses money, and the reflection is gloomy.
explanation.walkthrough: LEAN holds V to make LEVAN, which reversed spells NAVEL. 'Depression' here is a physical hollow, not a mood.
explanation.definitionFit: The navel is a small hollow or dip in the belly, so it is literally a depression in the body.

clue.text: Skyscraper maintenance issues? Jerks may apply elsewhere

definitions.text: Skyscraper maintenance issues? Jerks may apply elsewhere

parts.note: surface reading: problems keeping a tall building running, such as elevators that have stopped working
setter's reading: weightlifting exercises, which are separate from the clean and jerk, a different lift done elsewhere in training

explanation.walkthrough: The first half pictures broken elevators in a tower block; the second half shifts to the gym, where the jerk is one lift and this is another.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadlift is a weightlifting exercise raising a barbell from the floor, and a lift that has died is a broken elevator.

clue.text: Not entirely remarkable English story

indicators.note: not entirely means the word is incomplete, missing its final letter

parts.note: a tall story is a remarkable, hard-to-believe one
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A story told in English that is only partly remarkable.
explanation.walkthrough: TALL loses its last letter to give TAL, then E is added.
explanation.definitionFit: A tale is a narrative or story, especially an invented one.

clue.text: Pass time surrounded by swirling aurora — lots of decorative stuff here

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass

indicators.note: something surrounded is enclosed, so the time letter sits inside the other letters
swirling suggests letters whirled about and landing in a new order

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone passes the time under a swirling aurora, a sky full of ornamental colour.
explanation.walkthrough: The colourful sky scene suggests visual decoration, but the decoration meant is musical: florid runs and trills in singing.
explanation.definitionFit: Coloratura is elaborate ornamentation in vocal music, with runs and trills, so a passage full of it is highly decorated.

clue.text: Having debauched line with coitus?

indicators.note: debauched means corrupted and led astray, so the letters are knocked out of order

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A cheeky question about someone with a rakish chat-up line and a taste for sex.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer as well as building it: debauched both mixes the letters and describes the behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Licentious means sexually unrestrained and dissolute, exactly the debauched conduct the clue sketches.

clue.text: Part of skeleton in cupboard looks originally a crime involving lake

indicators.note: originally points to how each word begins, so only initial letters count

parts.note: the opening letters of these two words

indicators.note: involving means taking something in, so the crime wraps round the next item

parts.note: a vice is a crime or wrongdoing
L is the abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A skeleton in the cupboard looks like the trace of an old crime near a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface plays on the idiom a skeleton in the cupboard, a hidden scandal; here the skeleton is literal and the definition is a bone.
explanation.definitionFit: The clavicle, or collarbone, is one of the bones making up the human skeleton.

clue.text: Treatment for poison never used in Vietnam, sadly

indicators.note: sadly means in a sorry state, so the letters end up in disarray

parts.note: no, as in no way, stands for never
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lament that snakebite remedies were never available in wartime Vietnam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Never used in' reads as a history lesson, but never only supplies two letters to join the country's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Antivenom is the antibody serum given to counteract a snake or spider venom.

clue.text: I'm taken aback during religious sermon

indicators.note: during means in the middle of, so the reversed letters sit inside the next word

parts.note: holy means religious or sacred

indicators.note: taken aback is read literally as carried backwards, so the letters run in reverse

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A churchgoer admits being startled during a religious address.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken aback' reads as startled, but it is meant literally: carried backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A homily is a sermon or religious talk, often a short moralising one.

clue.text: Confusion about web and about conifer

indicators.note: about means around, so the confusion word encloses the web word

parts.note: pie, or printer's pie, is a jumbled mess of type
a net is a web, and the Net is the World Wide Web
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Muddle over the internet, and about some evergreen tree.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue uses about twice: first as a wrapping signal, then for a two-letter word meaning concerning. Printer's pie is spilled, jumbled type.
explanation.definitionFit: A pine is a coniferous evergreen tree with needles and cones, so a pine tree is a conifer.

clue.text: Woman's pursuing scoundrel? You bet!

indicators.note: pursuing means following behind, so the woman's word comes after the other

parts.note: a rat is a scoundrel or traitor
her stands for a woman, with the 's read as is

explanation.surface: Is a woman chasing a rogue? Certainly she is.
explanation.walkthrough: Woman's is read as woman is, a common contraction trick in clues.
explanation.definitionFit: Rather! is an old-fashioned British exclamation of emphatic agreement, much like saying certainly or of course.

clue.text: Jewellery item allowed in decorative hair

parts.note: a ring is a piece of jewellery
let means allowed

explanation.surface: A jewel permitted to be worn in an elaborate hairstyle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like it puts something inside, but it only links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A ringlet is a long spiral curl of hair, a styled and ornamental lock.

clue.text: Poor and indistinct, going round and round front of garage at the end of the day

indicators.note: going round turns each word to face the other way, and the repetition covers both words

parts.note: dim means faint or indistinct

indicators.text: and indistinct, going round and round
indicators.note: going round also means encircling, so the second word wraps the single letter

parts.note: a thin excuse is a poor one

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the opening letter of garage

explanation.surface: A dim, faltering motorist circles the garage forecourt as the day closes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going round and round' does double duty: both words turn backwards, and the second goes round the garage letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Midnight is twelve o'clock at night, the point when one day finishes and the next begins.

clue.text: Proposition those people to accept output of quarry

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so the people word wraps round the quarry product

parts.note: them refers to those people
ore is the mineral dug out of a mine or quarry

explanation.surface: A business proposal asking a group to take the stone produced by a quarry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Proposition' suggests an offer, but here it is the mathematical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics a theorem is a proposition that can be proved from axioms.

clue.text: Team from Southampton isn't seen aboard ship

indicators.note: aboard a ship means inside it, so the word goes within the ship letters

parts.note: SS is the abbreviation for steamship
ain't is a colloquial form of isn't

explanation.surface: A football side from the port of Southampton never seen on board ship.
explanation.walkthrough: Southampton FC is an English football club whose nickname is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Saints is the long-standing nickname of Southampton Football Club.

clue.text: Disciple turned to welcome corrupt neophytes

indicators.note: to welcome someone is to take them in, so the reversed word encloses the next
turned means faced the other way, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: a son is a disciple or follower of a master, as in a spiritual son
to vitiate is to spoil or corrupt

explanation.surface: A follower who changed sides takes in corrupt beginners.
explanation.walkthrough: A son as a disciple is the old sense of a spiritual son or follower of a teacher; vitiate means to spoil or impair.
explanation.definitionFit: Novitiates are novices, newcomers to a religious order, which is what neophytes are.

clue.text: Dismal nonsense dismissing a Government

indicators.note: dismissing means sending away, so the named letters are taken out

parts.note: blague is humbug or nonsense, a word borrowed from French
taken as written
G is the abbreviation for government

explanation.surface: A gloomy verdict: it's all rubbish, so get rid of the government.
explanation.walkthrough: BLAGUE loses A and G to leave BLUE. Blague is an uncommon word, so this one leans on the crossing letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue in the sense of sad or depressed is a common synonym for dismal.

clue.text: Body chemical, with iodine and phosphorus, found in part of eye

indicators.note: found in means located inside, so the element letters go within the eye part

parts.note: the lid, or eyelid, is part of the eye
P is the chemical symbol for phosphorus
I is the chemical symbol for iodine

explanation.surface: A biochemistry note on a compound containing iodine and phosphorus located in the eye.
explanation.walkthrough: I and P go inside LID.
explanation.definitionFit: Lipids are fats and related organic compounds that are essential chemicals in the body.

clue.text: Depth vessel, as in the hadal zone?

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for depth
an ark is a vessel, like Noah's

explanation.surface: A deep-sea craft exploring the hadal zone, the ocean's deepest trenches.
explanation.walkthrough: The hadal zone is the deepest part of the ocean, below about 6,000 metres, where no sunlight reaches; the question mark marks the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: No light penetrates to the deepest ocean trenches, so conditions there are pitch black.

clue.text: Person of property's path runs around upland

indicators.note: around means encircling, so the path and runs enclose the next word

parts.note: a lane is a narrow path or road
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
a down is an area of open upland, as in the South Downs

explanation.surface: A rich person's track winds round the high ground of their estate.
explanation.walkthrough: The downs are rolling chalk hills in southern England, so a down is upland. The 's is read as is, linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A landowner is someone who owns land, the classic person of property.

clue.text: A sailor keeping power right on standard setting

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: keeping means holding on to, so the sailor encloses the letter for power

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor
P is the abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: A sailor keeps the engine power exactly at its normal setting.
explanation.walkthrough: TAR takes P after its first letter. The definition reads as exactly on the standard level, as with shares trading at face value.
explanation.definitionFit: At par means at the nominal or face value, so precisely on the standard level set.

clue.text: Obligations to hold on to money in contemporary conditions

indicators.note: to hold on to something is to keep it within, so the obligations enclose the next item

parts.note: ties are bonds or obligations
M is the abbreviation for money

explanation.surface: In today's world, duties force people to cling on to their cash.
explanation.walkthrough: TIES goes round M.
explanation.definitionFit: The times, as in a sign of the times, means the prevailing state of affairs in the present age.

clue.text: His home, with King and Duke, possibly a hereditary state

indicators.note: possibly signals one arrangement among many, so the letters may be reordered

parts.note: taken as written
K is the chess abbreviation for king
D is the abbreviation for duke

explanation.surface: A noble's home, shared with a king and a duke, might be a realm passed down by birth.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheikhdom is a territory ruled by a sheikh, with rule usually passing down through the family.
